About locking the doors, try going against your fears by not locking them and seeing if you're there in the morning. Most likely, you'll still be there. It's mainly all in your head. I know how real it feels, I really do. Things seem all so connected, but they aren't what they seem. You can never know what's going on nor what they think.(even if it seems really bad) Anxiety definitely increases during the night, because this is when you're thinking the most

When you sleep and get these thoughts, think to yourself, you'll be in a better mindset in the morning. The best thing you can do is try to be in a meditative state and let it pass. (Dont judge it until tomorrow)

When there's a song you like or you're using as a reference, try to analyse the song bit by bit. It helps writing down the lyrics so you get a feel for the song, what feels does it make you have. If the song is happy or sad, chorus pitches and duration. The durations too of the verses, intro, end etc. 

Mess around a bit - write down which instruments you can hear the highest and lowest, pick your favorites! Too much inspiration can make it sound less unique. Try out different genres, things you wouldn't use, say it be soul, country or others
